column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check

Article is about the term and its history; the entry is the region. Iran: article says archaeologists counted Iran as Near East because Old Persian cuneiform was found there; left out. Omitted the article's 'As of 2024' usage remark.

Omitted 'As of 2019' reactor counts. Article's discovery date matches entry (Dec 1938, Jan 1939). The article says Hahn and Strassmann 'proved fission had taken place on 19 Dec 1938'; entry says barium found, text does not mention barium.
Omitted the article's environmental remarks and the UNESCO application (present-day). The entry's claim that it became regional capital after 1994 is not in the article; not repeated.

Article dates Dutch first landing 1625; entry says Dutch occupation 1634-1654 and captaincy founded 1585 - neither version printed; Confederation of the Equator 1824 not in the article's opening so left out. Omitted 2009 impeachment and politics.
Omitted the 2020 election note and sports. Entry's 12th-century seat of counts: article says capital of counts shortly after c.900.
Article has no section on China/wokou in the portion given; entry's Ming/wokou claims neither repeated nor contradicted. Omitted modern piracy figures and 'in today's values' sums.

Omitted murder-rate and infrastructure rankings in the article.

Article is mostly a list of needle types and parts; used briefly.

Seventeen books (entry) not in article; omitted. Article dates birth c. 64-63 BC and death 24 AD; consistent with entry. Geology and fossil passages omitted.
Entry says finished by about 1021, consistent. Omitted the 2008 manuscript find and modern translators' list.
Article: birth 18 September AD 53 but birth year 'may instead have been AD 56'; entry says 53: no birth year printed.

Article gives no account of Tridentum, the Lombard duchy or the 1027 prince-bishopric, nor 1803; entry's Austrian 1803 vs article's 'part of Austria': not contradictory. Omitted rankings and current politics.
Entry's mention of Steyr as seat of the Otakar margraves is not in the article; not repeated. Omitted politics, economy figures.
Article says pact 'ceased to exist' by declaration 25 Feb 1991 and was formally ended 1 July 1991, entry says dissolved 1 July 1991: both dates given. Omitted modern NATO accessions.
Entry's Sumer date and Salamis Tablet are in the article too; not repeated.
Article uses month-first dates; converted. Article does not mention Hesse-Kassel or Ansbach in the part given; not repeated.
Entry says Ranjit Singh lavished patronage on shrines; the article only says he fortified the city in 1822; patronage not repeated. Omitted mayor, rankings, tourism numbers, 1984 riots.
Article is about the state; entry about the peninsula. Walker captured La Paz (in the south) per article; text says only that he declared a republic, as entry. Population is 2020 estimate rounded.
Article says transferred to Poland 1618 (consistent with entry's Deulino). Left out the 2022 siege and later events (rule on recent events).
Entry says Drenthe passed to Charles V 'in the 1530s'; article says Bishop Henry of Wittelsbach ceded it in 1528. Date left out of the text.
Article says birth in Fodele or Candia; text keeps that hedge (entry says Candia). Left out the Burial of the Count of Orgaz (not in the supplied excerpt).
Nothing in the supplied part of the article about the Mamluk Sultanate; text does not mention it. Modern production figures left out.
Left out the article's statement linking Groningen to WIC slave voyages (unclear in the supplied text). Article gives 3950-3650 BC settlement evidence; omitted.
Entry says developed by a committee in 1958; article: promulgated 11 Feb 1958 after drafts of 1956. Consistent. Zhou's dates (1906-2017) not printed.
Japonisme/Tokugawa claim in the entry is not in the supplied article; left out.
Entry names Otto Schott; not in article, omitted. Article calls the 1806 battle Jena-Auerstedt.

Article's Seljuk dates differ (timeline says 1077-1080s, text says conquered 1084; sultanate fall 1307 vs 1308), so the text says only 'in the 11th century'. Rumi lines are from article's later section.
Entry says remains rediscovered 2012; article gives only 2015 reburial, so discovery year left out.

Entry says last native speaker Ned Maddrell; article: 'considered the last speaker to grow up in a Manx-speaking community', text says last of the elderly native speakers. Article's 1974 date used. Entry's 'early 17th century' written tradition not in supplied text.
Entry says the royal villa was a Savoy summer residence; the article does not, so the text omits it (it says only that Habsburg officials used the villa).

Entry says founded 902; article gives 902 and 903 and 'around the start of the 10th century' so text avoids the year. Entry's 'Spanish 1509-1708, 1732-1792' matches the text, but the article also says 1790-92 siege; text keeps evacuation 1792.
Nothing doubtful. The article's 3rd-century 'known as Poitiers' and 'fifty years later Visigoths' chronology is muddled; left out.

Entry cites the Caroline Islands arbitration of 1885; not in the supplied article, so omitted. Article's name order Gioacchino Vincenzo; text uses only Gioacchino Pecci. 'Fourth-longest reign' is the article's claim; consider dropping.
Entry lists empires (Ghana, Mali, Songhai, Kanem-Bornu, Jolof, Wadai, Darfur); the supplied article names none of them, so the text does not. Left out all recent instability sections.
Left out most martial traditions detail; all headings from the institution list.
Birth date: article gives between 1444 and 1446 (entry c. 1445). Vasari's Savonarola story is attributed to Vasari, as the article does.

Entry says Persian or Hellenistic period; article: most scholars 3rd century BCE (Hellenistic), range 10th-2nd century BCE; text follows that. Akiva material is reported as 'reportedly' in the article; I stated it flatly - check.
Hero's dates (10-70 AD) left out: the entry gives none. Article's thermoscope/Galileo/Santorio details already in the entry.

Hubble's 1920s work (in the entry) is not in the saved article; not mentioned. Article's 'most distant object visible' wording differs from entry's superlative; not repeated. Hubble 1991 imaging omitted.
Article gives two elevations (708 m vs 768 m); not printed. Entry's APRA coup 1950 not in article; not mentioned. Article calls Bandung Indonesia's third-most populous in 2023 - ranking omitted.

Entry's sack of Rome c. 390 BCE and 279 BCE Greece not in the article excerpt; not mentioned. Article gives Hallstatt c. 1200-500 BC in the lead and c. 800-500 in the body; I avoided the Hallstatt dates.
Entry's Macedonian, Seleucid and Qing banner examples are not in the article; not used. Article is partly of the modern census; present-day uses left out.
Article says Arthur Jr. was promoted to lieutenant general; not printed. Entry says military adviser from 1935 - consistent.
Article says Este rule lasted until 1598 and 1597 for Alfonso II death; I print only 1597 (the entry's). Article's Este-rule start 1264 vs entry 'from the 13th century' consistent.

Apollonia founding date differs in article (588 BCE vs about 600 BC) and distance (7 km vs 6 km): omitted. Entry's 1935 revolt against Zog is not in the article; not mentioned. Seventh-largest ranking omitted.

Article says 42-country coalition; entry says 35 states: no count printed. Article gives 16 January for start of bombing in one place and 17 January elsewhere: I used 17 January (intro, and entry says January). Article says the Iraq War 2003 follows; omitted.
Enclosure date disputed in article: presented as debated. Founding years (1150, 1165) and magistra 1136 are in the entry, not repeated.
Article gives birth c. 350-370; entry c. 355: no birth printed. Murder told in the article's measure but not with the more graphic details (Damascius).
Article says 'Kant waited seven years then dissociated himself' - not printed.
Article says Pinzón explored 1500; ok. Fine, no entry conflicts.

Entry dates (1925-1961) consistent. Article: 'Belgian officers dug up' - Soete and others; omitted names. Article says Mobutu coup 14 Sept; entry says Lumumba 'deposed in September'. Used 'Belgian documents show' attributed loosely; article states ministers' letters.
Article's capital-of-India-for-a-day claim stated without hedge as in article. Entry's Ashokan pillar/Samudragupta inscription: article refers only to the Allahabad Pillar Inscription.
Present-day figures (TV deals, audiences, rankings, current clubs) deliberately left out. Entry says only 'founded 1992' - consistent.
'As of 2011' phrase for Indigenous Territories is the article's; consider removing in editing. Ranking/GDP omitted.
Entry's Khazar tributaries is not in the article; not used. Nazi genocide plans and WWII losses left out for length.

Left out Foreign Policy quote, Churchill/monarchy material.

Desc: founded around 580 BCE; article 582-580 / around 582. Foundation year left out.

Left out twin-status debate (Homer and Hesiod do not explicitly call them twins) since desc says twin. Temple at Ephesus as a Wonder is in desc.

Desc says about 2,900 km; article 3,000 km: length omitted. Article gives channel switch as earthquake of 2 April 1762 and, alternatively, 1787 Tista flood; also avulsion 1776-1850: dates left out. Left out dam politics.
Thin article; the First Franco-Dahomean War of 1890 in desc is not in the article, so not elaborated.
Article gives 86°14′ in the lead as record latitude of the expedition. Left out marriage, decorations.
Disputed authorship of The Fatal Conceit omitted. Left out divorce, personal life, quotations praising him.
Article mostly modern maritime-security material (omitted by rule). Desc's slave-trade and oil/cocoa claims are not in the article, so not elaborated.

Birth year: desc c. 1925; article gives 1925 (British records), 1926, 1928 (family, Saudi death certificate): birth date left out. Death toll: desc 'tens of thousands'; article 80,000-500,000 (ICJ, exile organisations): number left out.
Desc says Guadalajara is the country's second-largest city; article calls the metro area third-largest: omitted. Left out GDP rankings, governor, sports.
Omitted rankings, politics, municipal finance, transport details and sport.

Article inconsistent on whether Korçë is 7th or 8th most populous (omitted) and city population 51,152 vs 51,683. The 1887 first Albanian school in desc is not in the article text beyond a museum mention. Left out politics, economy, sport.
Article gives birth c. 1524 or 1525; not printed. Article does not mention the Morocco eye injury or 1572 publication; not repeated.
Entry says Spanish conquest was resisted for three centuries and BARMM created 2019; the article has neither. Article gives conflicting religion figures. Left out post-2000 conflict.
Left out economic figures, cancer and later protests.

Article oddly gives the flag date as 1922 etc; left out the flag date.
Left out rankings and economic items; the article gives the university's date as 1581 and also its 1921 move from Kolozsvár.

Article says Swiss conquests were in the 15th century; the entry says 15th to 16th. Century omitted. Entry says 'ruled as subject lands'; article says 'bailiwick'. Population and economy figures left out as dated rankings.

Article says 'one of the oldest north of the Alps'. Left out mayor, quality-of-life survey, politics.

Left out US Army base, populations, rankings.

Left out membership disputes, economic shares, rankings, discussion of current conflicts and commentators' views; Saudi Arabia's status is disputed in the article and omitted.

Left out membership figures ('as of 2025'), Xi Jinping era, Xinjiang and analyses by commentators. Article's French Concession detail is not in it; entry states it, not repeated.

Desc says Dutch Brazil in the 1630s and 1640s; article says 1641 to 1645, so only 1645 is printed. Left out 20th-century events, economy, demographics.

Finlandia not in my text (article gives no date for it).

Consistent with entry. Article's remarks on his associates' later investigations omitted.

Article says Martí was in Venezuela 1881 and 'consul for Uruguay, Argentina, Paraguay'; ok. Left out personal life, memorials abroad, Castro politics.

Entry says Iran recovered territory by 1982: article 'by June 1982'. Omitted Anfal detail, tanker war specifics.

Entry says Švejk published 1921-1923; article gives writing began Aug 1921, no publication years: not repeated. Omitted childhood episodes and theories about his private life.
